To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present the first deep RL model that learns control policies directly from raw pixels, and that this model achieves state-of-the-art performance on seven Atari 2609 games.

we have successfully applied deep reinforcement learning to Atari 2600 game playing, that our model is able to learn control policies directly form raw pixels in the input, that our model outperforms all prior work on the Arcade Learning Environment (ALE), and that it is able to surpass a human expert on several of the games.

1) we have created a new algorithm, called Deep Q-Networks (DQNs), that is capable of learning to play Atari 2600 video games directly from high-dimensional sensor input using reinforcement learning; 2) DQN is able to outperform all previous approaches on 6 out of 7 games; and 3) DQN surpasses a human professional human on 3 out of 7 Atari games.

the question of whether it is possible to train a computer system to perform well at a variety of tasks without having to explicitly program each one.
the development of a general reinforcement learning method based on the deep architecture of artificial neural networks.
the problem of how to build machines that perceive their environments through sensors and learn to act upon them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DQN model outperformed all previous approaches on 6 out of 7 Atari games, and it surpassed a human expert on 3 games, which is a remarkable achievement.
the model is the first to successfully learn control directly from high-dimensional sensory input using reinforcement.

the authors have successfully demonstrated a new approach to deep learning that is able to learn to play a wide variety of video games from raw pixels, without any human input, and without any game-specific domain knowledge.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were the first to show that it is possible to learn control policies directly using raw pixels from the screen, without relying on hand-engineered features.
it is the first time we see a model that can successfully learn from raw sensory input using reinforcement.
we are the first to show that a deep neural network can learn to play Atari 2600.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to build an effective reinforcement learning agent, directly from high-dimensional sensory input using a general method.
a deep neural network with experience replay and raw pixels as input can achieve superhuman performance on several Atari games, without any prior information about game specific domain knowledge.
deep reinforcement learning can work well directly on visual inputs, and that our approach can succeed on challenging problems without requiring special designed features.
